service.name: flux-exchange
service.summary: Holds credentials, terminates channels, runs operations for many callers and records what happened. Its primary caller is an agent, not a human: people sign in to wire things up, and agents are what call operations all day.

capabilities.title: Read what this build could run
capabilities.summary: Every connector this deployment carries and every operation each one declares — what it is, what it costs, and what effects it has.

call.caller: Anyone. This route resolves no principal and takes no token.
call.note: One connector per entry, with the count of operations it declares; the operations themselves are at the same path under the connector id, at /api/catalogue/connectors/{id}/operations. It answers what exists, not what you may call — with no principal resolved every operation comes back admitted: null, which is a third value and not a refusal.

capabilities.title: Create a Service Account
capabilities.summary: A Service Account is a non-human principal of exactly one tenant. A signed-in human creates it and hands its one-time token to an App, Agent or automation.

call.caller: A signed-in human, from this console. Not the App or Agent that will use it — creating non-human identities is an operator action.
call.note: Send id, what to call the Service Account within the tenant, and expires_at, seconds since the Unix epoch. The expiry is never defaulted: a body without one is refused rather than given a lifetime this host picked. There is no tenant field, and there is nowhere one could be put — the tenant is read from the caller this host resolved, and a tenant in the body is ignored rather than honoured.
call.warn: The response carries the token, and it is shown once. This host keeps a verifier rather than the token, so nothing here can show it to you again. Lose it and mint another.

capabilities.title: Authenticate with a Service Account
capabilities.summary: Present the one-time token as a bearer credential and have this host resolve the Service Account in its tenant.

call.caller: The App, Agent or automation holding the Service Account token.
call.note: Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. A successful response identifies the principal as kind service_account and carries no credential material.
call.warn: A Service Account receives no authority merely by authenticating. Tenant grants still decide which declared operations and channels it may use.

capabilities.title: Discover usable operations
capabilities.summary: Read exactly the connected and granted operation bindings available to this resolved Service Account, with a stable generation for turn-boundary refresh.

call.caller: A Service Account presenting its bearer token.
call.note: The response contains only operation declarations and existing tenant-local connection labels that this principal can invoke. Its generation is content-addressed: retain the tool projection while it is unchanged and refresh only between turns when it changes.
call.warn: This is not the anonymous full catalogue or a connection-management surface. It accepts no tenant, credential, endpoint, runtime or authority selector.

capabilities.title: Manage connections and credentials
capabilities.summary: Inspect and wire this tenant’s connector instances while credential values remain write-only and every address is derived from the resolved principal’s tenant.

call.caller: An operator authorized for this tenant. Service Accounts and other automation do not receive connection-management authority.
call.note: The collection returns connector instances, labels, declared credential addresses and whether each credential is held, plus value-free supplier evidence. It never returns a credential or setting value.
call.warn: Writing or deleting connection state changes the authority later invocations use. Those verbs are operator-scoped independently of this readable collection entry point.

capabilities.title: Manage grants
capabilities.summary: Inspect and edit the tenant’s fail-closed policy over connector-declared risk, effects and idempotency rather than lists of operation names.

call.caller: An operator authorized for this tenant. An agent cannot read policy it could use to plan around a refusal and cannot widen its own authority.
call.note: The collection is the tenant’s current grant document. PUT replaces it and POST /api/grants/preview evaluates a proposed selector without saving it.
call.warn: With no admitted grant, invocation and inbound subscription refuse before credential material is read or vendor traffic is delivered.

capabilities.title: Call an operation
capabilities.summary: Name an operation and get a result, without naming a host, a credential or a tenant. The credential never crosses the boundary; the authority does.

call.caller: Any principal this host resolved, including a signed-in human or a Service Account presenting its bearer token.
call.note: {operation} is the catalogue’s own id, as served at /api/catalogue/connectors, and the body is that operation’s declared parameters verbatim — there is no envelope, no tenant, no connector, no host and no credential, because every one of those is derived from the operation and from the principal this host resolved. The answer carries sent and retryable as fields, because an HTTP status answers neither: a 502 does not say whether the vendor received it. A vendor’s own 4xx comes back as 200 with its response in content, unshaped — the vendor said no and we could not ask are different events. A host with no credential store bound runs nothing and says so.
call.warn: This route is gated by identity and by grant. An operation runs only if a grant your tenant holds admits it, decided from what the operation declares — its risk, its effects, its idempotency — rather than from a list of names; anything else is refused with 403 not_granted, before any credential is read and with nothing sent. Grants are held per tenant, and a signed-in human of that tenant edits them at PUT /api/grants, stating a connector and at most a risk level rather than a list of operation ids. An agent cannot write there and cannot read there either: a caller able to enumerate a tenant’s policy can plan around it, which is why a refusal here names the operation and never the rule that refused it. So a tenant nobody has granted anything still runs nothing at all — ask whoever holds the tenant for a grant that admits what you need.

capabilities.title: Receive a vendor’s events
capabilities.summary: Have this host terminate a vendor’s channel, verify what arrives against the connector’s declaration, and hand you a typed event.

call.caller: A resolved principal presenting its session cookie or bearer token.
call.note: Upgrade to WebSocket, then send {action:"subscribe",request_id,channel_id}. The channel id must belong to the principal’s tenant and its connector, binding and complete selected event set must be admitted by an inbound grant. Acknowledgements and refusals echo request_id; live event messages carry only the declared event envelope.
call.warn: Delivery is live and at-most-once: there is no replay or cursor. A subscriber that cannot keep up with its bounded queue is disconnected without stopping the vendor channel.

capabilities.title: Store and publish workflows
capabilities.summary: Author, validate and publish immutable tenant-local Flux Programs; triggers, conditions and schedules remain Program semantics rather than a second Exchange execution model.

call.caller: An operator authorized for this tenant. Agents invoke a published workflow through the ordinary operation and grant boundary; they do not mutate its stored Program.
call.note: The collection lists tenant workflow drafts and immutable published versions. Run records are read separately through /api/workflow-runs.
call.warn: Publishing freezes the Program and its derived requirements. It does not create a parallel trigger or scheduling runtime inside Exchange.

capabilities.title: Read back what you did
capabilities.summary: Read immutable workflow run status and value-free node events without exposing arguments, results or credentials in the structural trace.

call.caller: A signed-in human. Runs are selected only from the tenant on the resolved principal; there is no tenant field or tenant-shaped path.
call.note: The answer lists immutable workflow version, terminal status and editor node lifecycle events. Each event contains only node identity, source path, occurrence, phase and an optional selected branch. Invocation arguments and node values are never recorded there.

capabilities.title: Host Managed Agents
capabilities.summary: Run a model, authored loop and bounded operation and datasource capabilities as a Managed Agent inside an installed Flux App.
capabilities.withheld: Planned in X-108, “Host installed Flux Apps and Managed Agents.”

capabilities.title: Hold runtime leases
capabilities.summary: Hold a caller-grant-scoped pull resource until its holder releases it or its TTL passes.
capabilities.withheld: Planned in X-118, “Make leases own rich runtime resources.”
